title: Coarser AI robot planning helped only when feedback was less frequent
summary: In four controlled tasks on a physical Franka robot, using fewer steps to sample actions from a learned policy lowered success under frequent replanning but improved success when the robot executed a longer action sequence before checking again. A moving-target task still needed frequent feedback.
ai_technology: Flow-matching vision-language-action policies including π₀ and π₀.₅
organization: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 matched solver-by-horizon interventions, trajectory assessment and physical Franka experiments, Figure 5

evidence.tested: The study crossed two sampling depths and two execution horizons and ran 40 matched rollouts per setting for its physical evaluation.
evidence.unknown: The interaction was observed in the tested policies and tasks. It does not support coarse sampling as a general strategy for contact-rich or highly dynamic settings.
evidence.ai_role: Flow-matching control policies produce action trajectories with varied solver depths and replanning periods under matched evaluations.
